topic_tag: an eighteenth-century map of a kingdom
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Comparing it with other maps of its day, one historian describes the surveyor's map as, above all, ______.

worlds.passage: In 1790 a country surveyor published a map of the kingdom that went through eleven printings in twenty years. Rival maps showed the kingdom's roads and towns as they stood. The surveyor also drew, in dotted lines, a canal joining the kingdom's two great rivers and roads to three hill villages that he expected to grow on water power; the canal dug in 1840 follows his line, and the three villages became the kingdom's chief mill towns. Comparing it with other maps of its day, one historian describes the surveyor's map as, above all, ______.
worlds.explanation: The map drew a canal and village roads that did not yet exist, and decades later the canal followed his line and the villages grew as he expected, so the map was "prescient." "Provincial" fails because the map looked across the whole kingdom, joining its two great rivers. "Portable" fails because nothing is said about the map's size or how it was carried. "Rigorous" fails because what set the map apart was what it foresaw, not the care of its measurements.

provincial.quote: a canal joining the kingdom's two great rivers
provincial.why: the map's distinctive features span the whole kingdom, not one home district

portable.why: what distinguished the map was what it drew, not its physical form

rigorous.quote: that he expected to grow on water power
rigorous.why: the added features rest on his expectations about the future, not on careful measurement of what existed

worlds.passage: In 1790 a country surveyor published a map of the kingdom that went through eleven printings in twenty years. Rival maps gave each county space in proportion to its size. The surveyor's home county, one of the smallest, filled nearly half his sheet, down to its lanes, mills and ferries, while the rest of the kingdom shared the other half with only its largest towns marked, and nearly every printing was sold in that county's market towns. Comparing it with other maps of its day, one historian describes the surveyor's map as, above all, ______.
worlds.explanation: A map of the whole kingdom gave half its space to one small home county and was bought almost entirely there, so it was "provincial," centered on local concerns. "Prescient" fails because the map recorded what existed rather than anticipating anything. "Portable" fails because the passage describes the map's layout, not its size or form. "Rigorous" fails because the map shows most of the kingdom only in outline, with its largest towns.

prescient.quote: down to its lanes, mills and ferries
prescient.why: the map detailed things already there, foreseeing nothing

portable.why: the passage concerns how space on the sheet was divided, not whether the map could be carried

rigorous.quote: with only its largest towns marked
rigorous.why: most of the kingdom was sketched thinly, the opposite of careful, thorough coverage

worlds.passage: In 1790 a country surveyor published a map of the kingdom that went through eleven printings in twenty years. Rival maps were engraved on sheets a yard wide, meant to hang in a study or lie open on a library table. The surveyor printed his on linen in sixteen panels hinged to fold flat, and the copies that survive, most of them owned by cattle drovers and traveling merchants, are worn through along the folds. Comparing it with other maps of its day, one historian describes the surveyor's map as, above all, ______.
worlds.explanation: Unlike wall and table maps, the surveyor's folded linen map went on the road with drovers and merchants, who wore it out along its folds, so it was "portable." "Prescient" fails because the passage says nothing about the map anticipating later events. "Provincial" fails because it was used by people traveling the kingdom, and nothing suggests it favored one district. "Rigorous" fails because the passage describes the map's form and use, not the accuracy of its survey.

prescient.quote: printed his on linen in sixteen panels
prescient.why: the map's distinction lay in its material and folding, not in foreseeing anything

provincial.why: its users carried it across the kingdom, giving no sign of a narrowly local outlook

rigorous.why: the evidence concerns how the map was carried and handled, not how carefully it was measured

worlds.passage: In 1790 a country surveyor published a map of the kingdom that went through eleven printings in twenty years. Rival maps copied their coastlines and roads from older charts, errors and all. The surveyor walked every main road with a measuring chain and fixed each town by sightings of the stars, and when the government's survey checked his sheets with better instruments sixty years later, few of his distances were off by more than a mile. Comparing it with other maps of its day, one historian describes the surveyor's map as, above all, ______.
worlds.explanation: Where rivals copied old errors, the surveyor measured every road and fixed every town himself, and a later survey found his distances nearly exact, so the map was "rigorous." "Prescient" fails because the map recorded what existed accurately rather than anticipating what would come. "Provincial" fails because his measurements covered the whole kingdom. "Portable" fails because nothing is said about the map's size or how it was carried.

prescient.quote: few of his distances were off
prescient.why: the later check confirms the accuracy of existing distances, not a prediction

provincial.why: the survey covered the kingdom's roads evenly, not one home district

portable.quote: fixed each town by sightings of the stars
portable.why: the passage concerns how the map was made accurate, not its physical form
